clue.text: Bounty's captain loses head with drunkard — a noted farce?

indicators.note: losing its head means the surname drops its opening letter

parts.note: Captain William Bligh commanded HMS Bounty at the time of the famous mutiny
a toper is a habitual heavy drinker

explanation.surface: A sea captain sails off with a drunk in what sounds like a comic opera plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses head' strips the B from BLIGH, leaving LIGH; 'with' simply joins it to TOPER and A.
explanation.definitionFit: A light opera is a comic musical stage work, so a farce set to music; the question mark flags the pun on 'noted'.

clue.text: What's left, say, in flimsy surroundings

indicators.note: 'in' places the abbreviation for 'say' within the word for flimsy
'surroundings' confirms that the flimsy word forms the outer wrapping here

parts.note: lacy fabric is delicate and flimsy
eg, for example, is the usual crossword signal from 'say'

explanation.surface: Something left behind, perhaps, wrapped up in delicate packaging.
explanation.definitionFit: A bequest is literally what someone has left to others in a will.

clue.text: Scrawny mob put on plays — nothing odd about that

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece put on another sits above it, so the mob comes first

parts.note: a mob is a gang of people

indicators.note: nothing odd about the word means its odd-numbered letters are removed, keeping only the even ones

explanation.surface: A thin crowd stages theatre, and the speaker sees nothing strange in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a person who is thin and bony, a synonym pair.

clue.text: Trio of distant objects for less than a penny

parts.note: a trio is a group of three
distant means far away
objects are things

explanation.surface: Three faraway objects bought for under a penny.
explanation.walkthrough: A farthing was an old British coin worth a quarter of a penny, so three of them made three-quarters of a penny.
explanation.definitionFit: Three quarter-penny coins totalled three-quarters of a penny, an amount just short of one penny.

clue.text: Group chasing Poldark getting upset, one owns

indicators.note: chasing means coming after, so the group's word goes before the other piece

parts.note: a posse is a group of people, originally one gathered to chase outlaws

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the first name is read backwards

parts.note: Ross Poldark is the hero of the Cornish novels and British TV drama Poldark

explanation.surface: A band of riders pursues the TV hero Poldark, who is getting rattled.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upset' means turned upside down, so the name reads bottom to top; Poldark's first name is Ross.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoever owns something is its holder or owner, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Global tour

definitions.meaning: shaped like a globe, spherical or circular
a regular circuit of calls, like a milkman's or a golfer's circuit of the course

explanation.surface: A trip around the world.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both spherical in shape and a circuit of visits or stops.

clue.text: Drug from a police department

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of a British police force

explanation.surface: Narcotics seized by, or obtained from, the detectives.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang name for the hallucinogen LSD, a well-known street narcotic.

clue.text: Trick to appreciate good dancing

parts.note: a con is a trick or swindle
to appreciate in value is to gain

explanation.surface: A scam designed to make the most of a good thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appreciate' here means rise in value, not enjoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Performing the conga, a Latin line dance, is a form of dancing.

clue.text: Mess with attractive woman, the first one having left

parts.note: a dish is slang for an attractive person
Eve was the first woman in the Bible

explanation.surface: Trouble with a beautiful woman whose previous partner has walked out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' only joins EVE to L; 'left' is the abbreviation, not departure.
explanation.definitionFit: To mess up hair or clothing is to make it untidy, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Complaining to Heston finally about healthy meat dish

indicators.note: about means the complaining-plus-to-plus-letter string goes around the healthy word

parts.note: beefing is slang for grumbling or complaining
well means in good health

indicators.note: finally picks only the closing letter of the chef's name

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles to the chef Heston Blumenthal about a wholesome meat dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning', but it is the container signal: the healthy word sits inside the grumbling string. Heston Blumenthal is a famous British chef.
explanation.definitionFit: A classic preparation of fillet steak wrapped in pastry, a named example of a meat dish.

clue.text: One doomed daughter of Lear (not the Italian)

indicators.note: 'not' tells us to leave the Italian word out of the daughter's name

parts.note: Goneril is King Lear's eldest daughter in Shakespeare's play
il is the Italian for 'the'

explanation.surface: A doomed Shakespearean daughter, minus anything Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone beyond saving, certain to die or fail, is a lost cause, which the slang term means.

clue.text: Wine brewed nearest us

indicators.note: brewed suggests ingredients mixed together, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wine made at the vineyard closest to us.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet white dessert wine from Bordeaux, a specific example of wine.

clue.text: School cricket side hosted by old king

indicators.note: hosted by means held inside the king's name

parts.note: Old King Cole of the nursery rhyme
the leg side is the half of a cricket field behind the batsman's legs

explanation.surface: A school cricket team entertained by an elderly monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the leg (or on) side is the half of the field on the batsman's legs side.
explanation.definitionFit: An institution of learning, such as a sixth-form or university body, is a kind of school.

clue.text: Let down seeing scenery set in river

indicators.note: set in means placed inside the river's name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
a flat is a framed piece of stage scenery

explanation.surface: Disappointed by the view of scenery beside a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To let down a tyre or balloon is to let the air out of it, a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Fresh trainees hate to increase risk

indicators.note: fresh suggests a new version, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: New recruits dislike taking bigger chances.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker, upping the stake each player must put in raises what is at risk; idiomatically, to escalate stakes.

clue.text: Offer to take trouble in number 10?

indicators.note: to take means the offer word swallows the trouble word

parts.note: a tender is a formal offer
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A proposal to sort out problems at Number 10 Downing Street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number 10' suggests the Prime Minister's residence, but in cricket the tenth batsman is a weak lower-order hitter.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricketer batting near the bottom of the order, such as at number ten, is described this way.

clue.text: Small pack endlessly trumpeted as thing to do with eggs?

parts.note: to cram is to pack tightly

indicators.note: endlessly means the past-tense word loses its final letter

parts.note: blew, as one blows a trumpet

explanation.surface: A small pack of hounds announces breakfast with a trumpet blast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts the W from BLEW, leaving BLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Whisking and cooking eggs in a pan is one way of preparing them, so it is something done with eggs.

clue.text: Intended following of French resistance

indicators.note: following means the intended comes after the French word

parts.note: de is French for 'of'
one's intended is one's fiancé

explanation.surface: A betrothed partner involved with the French Resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: Open refusal to obey is a form of resistance, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Oppressed heretics fled somewhere in Derbyshire

indicators.note: oppressed suggests being knocked about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Persecuted heretics escaped to a refuge in Derbyshire.
explanation.definitionFit: A market town in the English county of Derbyshire, known for its crooked church spire.

clue.text: Burning a briquette initially to use no energy

indicators.note: initially takes just the opening letter of the fuel block

parts.note: to laze is to idle and expend no effort

explanation.surface: Set alight, a fuel block burns without needing any extra energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on fire and flaming fiercely is burning, a synonym.

clue.text: Economic slump, losing one third when Parliament's not sitting

indicators.note: losing one third means the last three of the nine letters are dropped

parts.note: a recession is a period of economic decline

explanation.surface: A downturn cuts the economy by a third while MPs are on holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: The holiday period of a legislature, when it does not meet, is its break.

clue.text: A fashionable set in function that's senseless

indicators.note: set in means placed inside the function's name

parts.note: sine is a trigonometric function
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: A trendy crowd at a party that makes no sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Silly and foolish, lacking any sense, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Guard overlooking small gate

indicators.note: overlooking means ignoring, so the small letter is left out

parts.note: a sentry is a soldier on guard

explanation.surface: A sentry on duty, watching over a little gate.
explanation.definitionFit: A way in, such as a gateway or door, is an access point.

clue.text: Make lord over in novel bonnet

indicators.note: in an across clue, over means turned around, so those letters are read right to left
'in' says the letters sit inside the words novel bonnet

explanation.surface: A lord made, dressed in an unusual bonnet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' finds ELBONNE inside 'novel bonnet', and 'over' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise someone to the peerage, giving them a title, is the sense of the verb.

clue.text: Get behind with revising, being ignorant

indicators.note: revising means reworking, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A student falls behind on exam revision and stays ignorant.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally overtaken by darkness, figuratively living in intellectual or moral darkness, unenlightened.

clue.text: Kid needs afternoon snacks to get energy

parts.note: afternoon teas are light meals of sandwiches and cake
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A child needs a teatime snack to get a burst of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' looks like a child, but it is the verb meaning to joke with someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To kid someone is to rib or make fun of them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Pitcher of Milwaukee Brewers

indicators.note: 'of' signals that the answer is part of the team's name, drawn from inside it

explanation.surface: A baseball pitcher on the Milwaukee Brewers team.
explanation.walkthrough: The Brewers are a US baseball team, so 'Pitcher' looks like a player.
explanation.definitionFit: A large wide-mouthed jug for water is called a pitcher.

clue.text: Cover up QPR broadcast bloomers

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken on air, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: to cover up is to hide, and QPR is Queens Park Rangers, a London football club, giving hide Rangers

explanation.surface: A scandal at QPR is hushed up on air.
explanation.definitionFit: Garden shrubs with large flower heads are plants that bloom, so playfully bloomers.
